subject: Proposal: accelerated commit conversion & rate path for Elara Health
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Avery <tom.avery@elarahealth.com>, Elara Contracts <contracts@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Nov 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: accelerated commit conversion & rate path for Elara Health

Tom / Contracts team —

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, Elara's production traffic is consistently above the current monthly commit and you're seeing repeated soft-throttle events during peak hours. I've attached a formal proposal that lays out a staged conversion from your current burst-heavy plan into a higher committed monthly tier with a predictable rate band and an explicit overage staircase. Key points in the attachment:

- 6-month phased commit increase (1.5x month 1, 2x month 3, 2.5x month 6)
- Rate band smoothing for token pricing as commit increases
- Reserved throughput window for batch job windows (00:00–04:00 PT)
- One-time migration credit to offset prorated first-month fees

I'll summarize the financials inline so procurement can quickly compare it to your current invoices. If this looks sensible, we can kick off procurement + legal and aim for a Dec 15 go-live for the first uplift.

Attachment: Elara_commit_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference for product teams

From: Tom Avery <tom.avery@elarahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Nov 2029 11:05:14 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: accelerated commit conversion & rate path for Elara Health

Marcus —

Appreciate the write-up. Initial read looks promising. A couple of quick Qs for procurement: 

1) That migration credit — is it applied as a one-time invoice credit or as an upfront discount on the first month? We prefer a credit line on the invoice so our accounting team sees the adjustment.
2) Can you confirm the SLA/latency target for the reserved throughput window? We run large batching at 01:00 PT and need predictable tail-latency.

Also looping in our internal procurement alias (contracts@elarahealth.com) so we can get your SOW and an estimated invoice schedule.

If everything lines up, we should be able to approve before Dec 10.

—Tom
Tom Avery | Head of Platform Engineering, Elara Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elara Contracts <contracts@elarahealth.com>, Tom Avery <tom.avery@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Nov 2029 08:44:22 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: accelerated commit conversion & rate path for Elara Health

Tom — quick answers inline and a short ops/finance summary below.

On Nov 20, 2029 at 11:05 AM Tom Avery <tom.avery@elarahealth.com> wrote:
> 1) That migration credit — is it applied as a one-time invoice credit or as an upfront discount on the first month? We prefer a credit line on the invoice so our accounting team sees the adjustment.

We can do a one-line invoice credit that appears on month 1 — that's our standard for migration incentives. I'll confirm the exact GL/description with billing and include the wording in the SOW.

> 2) Can you confirm the SLA/latency target for the reserved throughput window? We run large batching at 01:00 PT and need predictable tail-latency.

Reserved window SLA: 99.9% of inference requests in the reserved window will have 90th-percentile latency <= 250ms for payloads <= 1k tokens when using a supported model variant. That's with the dedicated soft-reserve we propose in the doc. For mission-critical batch jobs we can also add an 'ops escalation' contact during the 00:00–04:00 PT window.

Short financial summary (visible in redwood-ratebands-v3.xlsx attached):
- Current estimated monthly commit: 3.2M tokens
- Proposed committed tiers: 4.8M / 6.4M / 8.0M (months 1 / 3 / 6)
- Blended per-token rate (post-conversion) starts at $0.0011 and steps down to $0.00095 at the 8.0M tier
- One-time migration credit: $12,000 as invoice credit on first month

Next steps we propose:
1) I share a short SOW + invoice cadence doc (1 page) for procurement to sign.
2) Legal to run a quick redline — I can accept standard SLAs but will need a limited liability cap consistent with our team guidelines.
3) Ops runbook for reserved window handoff (we'll schedule a 30-minute runbook review with your SREs after PO).

I'll drop the SOW into Drive and ping here when it's live.

Thanks —
Marcus

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Nov 2029 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Elara procurement expectations / legal checklist (do not forward)

Marcus / Steph —

Notes from counsel/procurement after reviewing the proposal: 
- Legal wants the SOW to explicitly call out the invoice credit mechanics and the proration calculation for month 1. They asked for sample invoice wording.
- Procurement requested net-45 payment terms but Elara's finance team historically accepts net-30; we should be prepared to offer net-30 with an early-pay 1% discount for net-15.
- Ask legal to limit liability cap to "amounts paid in the prior 12 months" rather than a blanket multiple — they'll accept that.
- Ops: confirm that the reserved window SLA calls out model variants (we should enumerate supported models in the SOW addendum).

I'll draft a 1-page SOW and invoice example this afternoon and share the Drive link. Marcus — please include the runbook owners (Ops contact) before you send to Elara.

-Kim
Kimberly Park | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Avery <tom.avery@elarahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Dec 2029 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: accelerated commit conversion & rate path for Elara Health

Marcus / Kim —

Thanks — the team reviewed the numbers and the SLA language looks good. We can accept the staged commit conversion and the invoice credit as a line item. Procurement asked for the SOW and a final invoice schedule so they can cut the PO; Tom B. in finance (tom.brennan@elarahealth.com) is ready to be looped in on a PO template.

Please go ahead and share the SOW + final invoice cadence and I'll route to Tom B. for PO issuance. Targeting PO by Dec 10.

—Tom
